chart bugfix: value-label/category-label collision on two JS-built waterfall charts
version_history.note: This post's charts are built at runtime by inline JS (string-concatenated SVG injected via innerHTML), which tools/svg_chart_lint.py cannot parse (it flags a parse error on the literal '+W+' JS-templating text) -- so this fix was found by rendering the full page in a headless browser (letting the JS execute) and visually inspecting each chart, not by the linter. The shared waterfall() function placed each bar's value label at a fixed offset below the bar's bottom edge; when a bar's bottom coincided with the chart's overall minimum (the exc-cur and exc-fut excise/VAT/exchequer charts, where the VAT and Net-exchequer bars both bottom out at the series minimum), that label collided with the category-name row underneath. Fixed by capping the label's y-position so it can never go below a safe margin above the category-label row, regardless of how close the bar's bottom sits to the plot's edge. Verified by re-rendering all 9 of this post's waterfall/bar charts; the previously-unaffected ones (all-positive bars, which use the top-of-bar label branch) are unchanged.
